description: Use this when the host wants to change an interview that already exists: its title, purpose, mode, language, first or closing message, questions, result fields, the integrity signals or the warm-up. Do not use it to make a new interview (suggest_interview, then create_interview) or to read the current setup (get_interview), or for an existing meeting or recording, an uploaded file, a contact lookup, scoring or ranking participants, or advice alone. Change an existing interview using its current setup from get_interview and the host's edits. Changes to questions or result_fields replace the complete list. Any edit to the setup (title, purpose, mode, language, intro, outro, questions or result_fields) needs both complete lists, questions and result_fields, because they replace what is saved. title, purpose, mode, language, intro and outro are optional and stay as they are when left out; null or an empty value clears the purpose context, intro or outro. Saving makes a new version of the interview. mode is video or audio: an audio interview needs only a microphone from the participant. integritySignals turns the integrity signals of a video interview on or off and needs no lists; an audio interview has no integrity signals, so asking for one is refused and nothing is changed. warmup turns the warm-up before the first question on or off, for a video or an audio interview, and needs no lists. A new language does not translate the questions: send them in that language with the complete lists.

integritySignals.description: Whether the integrity signals run for this video interview, such as false to turn them off. Optional: it stays as it is when left out. It is saved on its own, without questions or result_fields. An audio interview has no integrity signals: sending this for one is refused and nothing is changed.

interview_id.description: The interview's id, exactly as list_interviews or create_interview returned it in its structured data. It is for tool calls only: never show it to the host; name the interview by its title. Do not guess an id, and do not send a title or an email address in its place: if you do not have the id, call list_interviews.

intro.description: The first message, such as "Hello, I'm Tracy. I'll ask a few questions about your experience." Null or empty clears it. Tracy always opens with a fixed notice that she is an AI interviewer. It comes before your first message and cannot be changed.

language.description: The language the interview is held in: en (English), de (German), es (Spanish), fr (French), id (Indonesian), ja (Japanese), ko (Korean), nl (Dutch), vi (Vietnamese). Send the code, e.g. es for Spanish, not the name. Optional: en (English) is the default. It does not translate questions you send: write them in this language. On update_interview, changing it leaves the saved questions as they are, so send them again in the new language.

mode.description: How the participant joins: video (the default) or audio, where they need only a microphone and no camera. Send audio when the host asks for an audio interview or one without a camera; otherwise leave it out. Optional: video is the default.

outro.description: The closing message, such as "Thank you for your time. That was everything I wanted to ask." Null or empty clears it.

purpose.description: The host's answers, if they change. Both participants and goal are needed.

context.description: Extra context. Null or empty clears it.

goal.description: What the host wants to find out.

questions.description: The complete list of questions, in the order Tracy asks them. It replaces the saved list: a question left out is removed, so send every question that stays again, unchanged ones exactly as get_interview shows them (text and source).

source.description: suggested: as suggest_interview wrote it. edited: a suggestion the host changed. own: written by the host. Defaults to own. Do not leave a question marked suggested once its text has changed: use edited.

text.description: One question, worded as Tracy should ask it, e.g. "What was the hardest part of your last project?". Keep the host's wording when they gave it.

result_fields.description: The complete list of fields the result reports, in the order the result shows them. It replaces the saved list: a field left out is removed, so send every field that stays again, unchanged ones as get_interview shows them. If the questions are reordered or removed, check each from_question against the new list.

from_question.description: The 0-based position of the question this field comes from, in the questions list sent with it: 0 is the first question, 2 the third. The replies number questions from 1, so "from question 3" is 2 here. Leave it out for a field that comes from no single question.

hint.description: How to read the answer, if the name alone is not clear, e.g. Whole years, not counting internships.

name.description: What the result reports, e.g. Years of experience.

title.description: A new title, such as Senior backend engineer screening.

warmup.description: Whether the warm-up runs before the first question, such as true to turn it on. Optional: it stays as it is when left out. It is saved on its own, without questions or result_fields, and applies to a video and an audio interview alike.

name: update_interview
title: Update an interview
